name: Nullwear — Anti-Scan Clothing Movement
creator: Technical collective Membrane, the Gray Zone origin, Tier 1-2
description: A fashion movement built around garments incorporating BCI-scrambling weave patterns, biometric-deflecting surface treatments, thermal camouflage underlayers, and gait-disruption sole inserts — all designed to degrade corponation and municipal surveillance systems' ability to identify, track, or read the wearer. Nullwear began as pure survival technology in the Gray Zone and evolved into an aesthetic language with its own visual vocabulary: angular disruption patterns, matte non-reflective surfaces, deliberately ambiguous silhouettes. The look is immediately recognizable to anyone who knows what they're looking at.
cultural_impact: Nullwear's spread forced multiple iterations of municipal surveillance system upgrades, creating an ongoing arms race that has cost the city of GLMZ an estimated Φ2 billion over three decades. The movement also established anti-surveillance fashion as a legitimate design discipline, with academic programs now teaching its technical principles.
controversy: Corponation Axiom lobbied successfully for Nullwear materials to be classified as 'surveillance countermeasure devices' subject to registration and licensing in 2209, effectively criminalizing the movement for Tier 1 practitioners who cannot afford compliance while leaving wealthier buyers unaffected.
story_hooks: A Nullwear practitioner is the only person in the vicinity of a major crime who cannot be identified by any surveillance system — making them simultaneously a suspect and the only person who saw the truth.
The Membrane collective's newest anti-scan weave pattern has an unexpected side effect: it disrupts nearby BCIs, causing temporary memory dropout in anyone who stands too close.

A corponation begins manufacturing licensed 'fashion-grade' Nullwear that includes a back-channel transmission to their own systems — practitioners need to spread the word before it becomes the movement's dominant product.
